Informal Type serves as a parent property for string-valued properties meant to describe a type without implementing a class design.  This property hierarchy supports a balancing point between semantic specificity and operational agility.  The known benefits of describing types rather than implementing them include swift extensibility of some existing, or possibly non-existing, subclass hierarchy in UCO without requiring training in ontological development, taxonomic specification, or OWL, SHACL, or RDF maintenance logistics.  The known detractions of using string-literals for type descriptions include that used vocabularies may require careful maintenance among data-sharing parties; that vocabularies require independent logistics (external to UCO) for providing definitions (i.e., dictionary-style semantics) to string-literals chosen; and that string-literals cannot by themselves encode hierarchical structure or entailments, such as the informal device type string 'ExamplePhone 8 P4321' entailing 'ExamplePhone 8', 'ExamplePhone', or 'ExamplePhone models discontinued in 2020'.  Usage of Informal Type to house strings should be weighed against usage of classes when classes are available, and should periodically be reviewed for potential additions to UCO's class hierarchy or downstream extensions thereof.

A granular marking is a grouping of characteristics unique to specification of marking definitions (restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how data can be used and shared) that apply to particular portions of a particular UCO object.

A license marking is a grouping of characteristics unique to the expression of data marking definitions (restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how data can be used and shared) to convey details of license restrictions that apply to the data.

A marking definition is a grouping of characteristics unique to the expression of a specific data marking conveying restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how marked data can be used and shared.

A marking model is a grouping of characteristics unique to the expression of a particular form of data marking definitions (restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how data can be used and shared).

A release-to marking is a grouping of characteristics unique to the expression of data marking definitions (restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how data can be used and shared) to convey details of authorized persons and/or organizations to which to the associated content may be released. The existence of the Release-To marking restricts access to ONLY those identities explicitly listed, regardless of whether another data marking exists that allows sharing with other members of the community.

A statement marking is a grouping of characteristics unique to the expression of data marking definitions (restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how data can be used and shared) to convey details of a textual marking statement, (e.g., copyright) whose semantic meaning should apply to the associated content. Statement markings are generally not machine-readable. An example of this would be a simple marking to apply copyright information, such as 'Copyright 2014 Acme Inc.'.

A terms of use marking is a grouping of characteristics unique to the expression of data marking definitions (restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how data can be used and shared) to convey details of a textual statement specifying the Terms of Use (that is, the conditions under which the content may be shared, applied, or otherwise used) of the marked content. An example of this would be used to communicate a simple statement, such as 'Acme Inc. is not responsible for the content of this file'.
Specifies the identities that are authorized to access the data to which the data marking is associated.  The list of authorized identities are represented as UUIDs.

An API (application programming interface) is a computing interface that defines interactions between multiple software or mixed hardware-software intermediaries. It defines the kinds of calls or requests that can be made, how to make them, the data formats that should be used, the conventions to follow, etc. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API]

An ARP cache is a collection of Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) entries (mostly dynamic) that are created when an IP address is resolved to a MAC address (so the computer can effectively communicate with the IP address). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARP_cache]

An ARP cache entry is a single Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) response record that is created when an IP address is resolved to a MAC address (so the computer can effectively communicate with the IP address). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARP_cache]
An account is an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service.
An account authentication facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the mechanism of accessing an account.
An account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service.
An adaptor is a device that physically converts the pin outputs but does not alter the underlying protocol (e.g. uSD to SD, CF to ATA, etc.)
An address is an identifier assigned to enable routing and management of information.
An alternate data stream is data content stored within an NTFS file that is independent of the standard content stream of the file and is hidden from access by default NTFS file viewing mechanisms.

An alternate data stream facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to data content stored within an NTFS file that is independent of the standard content stream of the file and is hidden from access by default NTFS file viewing mechanisms.
An Android device is a device running the Android operating system. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system)]
An Android device facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an Android device. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Android_(operating_system)]
An android phone is a smart phone that applies the Android mobile operating system.
An antenna alignment facet contains the metadata surrounding the cell tower's antenna position.
An apple device is a smart device that applies either the MacOS or iOS operating system.
An appliance is a purpose-built computer with software or firmware that is designed to provide a specific computing capability or resource. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_appliance]
An application is a particular software program designed for end users.
An application account is an account within a particular software program designed for end users.
An application account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an account within a particular software program designed for end users.
An application facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular software program designed for end users.
An application version is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular software program version.
An archive file is a file that is composed of one or more computer files along with metadata.
An archive file facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a file that is composed of one or more computer files along with metadata.
Audio is a digital representation of sound.
An audio facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a digital representation of sound.

An autonomous system is a collection of connected Internet Protocol (IP) routing prefixes under the control of one or more network operators on behalf of a single administrative entity or domain that presents a common, clearly defined routing policy to the Internet. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_system_(Internet)]

An autonomous system facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a collection of connected Internet Protocol (IP) routing prefixes under the control of one or more network operators on behalf of a single administrative entity or domain that presents a common, clearly defined routing policy to the Internet. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_system_(Internet)]
A blackberry phone is a smart phone that applies the Blackberry OS mobile operating system. (Blackberry 10 re-introduces Blackberry OS, prior to that the OS was Android.)

A block device node is a UNIX filesystem special file that serves as a conduit to communicate with devices, providing buffered randomly accesible input and output. Block device nodes are used to apply access rights to the devices and to direct operations on the files to the appropriate device drivers. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_file_types]

A Bluetooth address is a Bluetooth standard conformant identifier assigned to a Bluetooth device to enable routing and management of Bluetooth standards conformant communication to or from that device.

A Bluetooth address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a Bluetooth standard conformant identifier assigned to a Bluetooth device to enable routing and management of Bluetooth standards conformant communication to or from that device.
A bot configuration is a set of contextual settings for a software application that runs automated tasks (scripts) over the Internet at a much higher rate than would be possible for a human alone.
A browser bookmark is a saved shortcut that directs a WWW (World Wide Web) browser software program to a particular WWW accessible resource. [based on https://techterms.com/definition/bookmark]

A browser bookmark facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a saved shortcut that directs a WWW (World Wide Web) browser software program to a particular WWW accessible resource. [based on https://techterms.com/definition/bookmark]
A browser cookie is a piece of of data sent from a website and stored on the user's computer by the user's web browser while the user is browsing. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_cookie]

A browser cookie facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a piece of data sent from a website and stored on the user's computer by the user's web browser while the user is browsing. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HTTP_cookie]
A calendar is a collection of appointments, meetings, and events.

A calendar entry facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an appointment, meeting, or event within a collection of appointments, meetings, and events.
A calendar facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a collection of appointments, meetings, and events.
A call is a connection as part of a realtime cyber communication between one or more parties.

A captured telecommunications information facet represents certain information within captured or intercepted telecommunications data.
A cell site facet contains the metadata surrounding the cell site.

A character device node is a UNIX filesystem special file that serves as a conduit to communicate with devices, providing only a serial stream of input or accepting a serial stream of output. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_file_types]

Code is a direct representation (source, byte or binary) of a collection of computer instructions that form software which tell a computer how to work. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software]
A compressed stream facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the application of a size-reduction process to a body of data content.

A computer is an electronic device for storing and processing data, typically in binary, according to instructions given to it in a variable program. [based on 'Computer.' Oxford English Dictionary, Oxford University Press, 2022.]
A computer specification is the hardware and software of a programmable electronic device that can store, retrieve, and process data. {based on merriam-webster.com/dictionary/computer]

A computer specificaiton facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the hardware and software of a programmable electronic device that can store, retrieve, and process data. [based on merriam-webster.com/dictionary/computer]
A ConfiguredSoftware is a Software that is known to be configured to run in a more specified manner than some unconfigured or less-configured Software.
A contact is a set of identification and communication related details for a single entity.
A contact address is a grouping of characteristics unique to a geolocation address of a contact entity.
A contact affiliation is a grouping of characteristics unique to details of an organizational affiliation for a single contact entity.
A contact email is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by email.
A contact facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a set of identification and communication related details for a single entity.
A contact list is a set of multiple individual contacts such as that found in a digital address book.
A contact list facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a set of multiple individual contacts such as that found in a digital address book.
A contact messaging is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by digital messaging.
A contact phone is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by telephone.
A contact profile is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by online service.
A contact SIP is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by Session Initiation Protocol (SIP).
A contact URL is a grouping of characteristics unique to details for contacting a contact entity by Uniform Resource Locator (URL).
Content data is a block of digital data.
A content data facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a block of digital data.
A cookie history is the stored web cookie history for a particular web browser.
A credential is a single specific login and password combination for authorization of access to a digital account or system.
A credential dump is a collection (typically forcibly extracted from a system) of specific login and password combinations for authorization of access to a digital account or system.
An DNS cache is a temporary locally stored collection of previous Domain Name System (DNS) query results (created when an domain name is resolved to a IP address) for a particular computer.
A DNS record is a single Domain Name System (DNS) artifact specifying information of a particular type (routing, authority, responsibility, security, etc.) for a specific Internet domain name.
A data range facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a particular contiguous scope within a block of digital data.
A defined effect facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the effect of an observable action in relation to one or more observable objects.
A device is a piece of equipment or a mechanism designed to serve a special purpose or perform a special function. [based on https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/device]

A device facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a piece of equipment or a mechanism designed to serve a special purpose or perform a special function. [based on https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/device]
A digital account is an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service within the digital domain.
A digital account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of some capability or service within the digital domain.
A digital address is an identifier assigned to enable routing and management of digital communication.
A digital address facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an identifier assigned to enable routing and management of digital communication.
A digital camera is a camera that captures photographs in digital memory as opposed to capturing images on photographic film.
A digital signature info is a value calculated via a mathematical scheme for demonstrating the authenticity of an electronic message or document.
A digital signature info facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a value calculated via a mathematical scheme for demonstrating the authenticity of an electronic message or document.

A directory is a file system cataloging structure which contains references to other computer files, and possibly other directories. On many computers, directories are known as folders, or drawers, analogous to a workbench or the traditional office filing cabinet. In UNIX a directory is implemented as a special file. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directory_(computing)]
A disk is a storage mechanism where data is recorded by various electronic, magnetic, optical, or mechanical changes to a surface layer of one or more rotating disks.

A disk facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a storage mechanism where data is recorded by various electronic, magnetic, optical, or mechanical changes to a surface layer of one or more rotating disks.

A disk partition is a particular managed region on a storage mechanism where data is recorded by various electronic, magnetic, optical, or mechanical changes to a surface layer of one or more rotating disks. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disk_storage]

A domain name is an identification string that defines a realm of administrative autonomy, authority or control within the Internet. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_name]

A domain name facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an identification string that defines a realm of administrative autonomy, authority or control within the Internet. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domain_name]
A drone, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), is an aircraft without a human pilot, crew, or passengers that typically involve a ground-based controller and a system for communications with the UAV.
Electronic Serial Number .

[based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exif]
An email account is an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of electronic mail (email) capabilities or services.
An email account facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to an arrangement with an entity to enable and control the provision of electronic mail (email) capabilities or services.
An email address is an identifier for an electronic mailbox to which electronic mail messages (conformant to the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)) are sent from and delivered to.

An email message facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a message that is an instance of an electronic mail correspondence conformant to the internet message format described in RFC 5322 and related RFCs.

An encoded stream facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the conversion of a body of data content from one form to another form.

An environment variable is a grouping of characteristics unique to a dynamic-named value that can affect the way running processes will behave on a computer. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environment_variable]
An event log is a collection of event records.
An event record is something that happens in a digital context (e.g., operating system events).
An event record facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to something that happens in a digital context (e.g., operating system events).
An extInode facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to a file system object (file, directory, etc.) conformant to the extended file system (EXT or related derivations) specification.
An extracted string is a grouping of characteristics unique to a series of characters pulled from an observable object.
An extracted strings facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to one or more sequences of characters pulled from an observable object.
A file is a computer resource for recording data discretely on a computer storage device.

A file facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the storage of a file (computer resource for recording data discretely in a computer storage device) on a file system (process that manages how and where data on a storage device is stored, accessed and managed). [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/Computer_file and https://www.techopedia.com/definition/5510/file-system]
A file permissions facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the access rights (e.g., view, change, navigate, execute) of a file on a file system.
A file system is the process that manages how and where data on a storage medium is stored, accessed and managed. [based on https://www.techopedia.com/definition/5510/file-system]

A file system facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the process that manages how and where data on a storage medium is stored, accessed and managed. [based on https://www.techopedia.com/definition/5510/file-system]
A file system object is an informational object represented and managed within a file system.

A forum post is message submitted by a user account to an online forum where the message content (and typically metadata including who posted it and when) is viewable by any party with viewing permissions on the forum.

A forum private message (aka PM or DM (direct message)) is a one-to-one message from one specific user account to another specific user account on an online form where transmission is managed by the online forum platform and the message is only viewable by the parties directly involved.

A named pipe is a mechanism for FIFO (first-in-first-out) inter-process communication. An operating system facet is a grouping of characteristics unique to the software that manages computer hardware, software resources, and provides common services for computer programs. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system]

A process thread is the smallest sequence of programmed instructions that can be managed independently by a scheduler on a computer, which is typically a part of the operating system. It is a component of a process. Multiple threads can exist within one process, executing concurrently and sharing resources such as memory, while different processes do not share these resources. A Windows critical section is a Windows object that provides synchronization similar to that provided by a mutex object, except that a critical section can be used only by the threads of a single process. Critical section objects cannot be shared across processes. Event, mutex, and semaphore objects can also be used in a single-process application, but critical section objects provide a slightly faster, more efficient mechanism for mutual-exclusion synchronization (a processor-specific test and set instruction). Like a mutex object, a critical section object can be owned by only one thread at a time, which makes it useful for protecting a shared resource from simultaneous access. Unlike a mutex object, there is no way to tell whether a critical section has been abandoned. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sync/critical-section-objects]
A Windows event is a notification record of an occurance of interest (system, security, application, etc.) on a Windows operating system.

A Windows file mapping is the association of a file's contents with a portion of the virtual address space of a process within a Windows operating system. The system creates a file mapping object (also known as a section object) to maintain this association. A file view is the portion of virtual address space that a process uses to access the file's contents. File mapping allows the process to use both random input and output (I/O) and sequential I/O. It also allows the process to work efficiently with a large data file, such as a database, without having to map the whole file into memory. Multiple processes can also use memory-mapped files to share data. Processes read from and write to the file view using pointers, just as they would with dynamically allocated memory. The use of file mapping improves efficiency because the file resides on disk, but the file view resides in memory.[based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/memory/file-mapping]

A Windows handle is an abstract reference to a resource within the Windows operating system, such as a window, memory, an open file or a pipe. It is the mechanism by which applications interact with such resources in the Windows operating system.

A Windows hook is a mechanism by which an application can intercept events, such as messages, mouse actions, and keystrokes within the Windows operating system. A function that intercepts a particular type of event is known as a hook procedure. A hook procedure can act on each event it receives, and then modify or discard the event. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/about-hooks]

A Windows mailslot is is a pseudofile that resides in memory, and may be accessed using standard file functions. The data in a mailslot message can be in any form, but cannot be larger than 424 bytes when sent between computers. Unlike disk files, mailslots are temporary. When all handles to a mailslot are closed, the mailslot and all the data it contains are deleted. [based on https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/about-mailslots]

A Windows network share is a Windows computer resource made available from one host to other hosts on a computer network. Network sharing is made possible by inter-process communication over the network. [based on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shared_resource]

Data obtained via Apple File Conduit (AFC) service from iOS devices.
Data that has been forensically collected from a source device or system. This is the parent class for all types of forensic data acquisition outputs.
Files associated with an AI chatbot or assistant application, including conversation histories, prompt logs, cached model responses, and user preference data (e.g. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini).
A contextual compilation of files associated with a specific application version. Groups the files belonging to a particular application (e.g. WhatsApp v13.2 database files) for forensic examination.
A contextual compilation of forensic artifacts grouped together for some purpose, such as filtering, redaction, or association with an investigation.
A file whose primary content is audio data (e.g. MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC).
A sequential, complete bit-for-bit copy of a storage medium (LBA0 to LBAmax). Represents data in transit from a capture process to a storage format.
Random access to sector-level data, whether from a live device or a decoded forensic image container. Enables partition parsing, filesystem traversal, and logical operations.
Files associated with a web browser application, including browsing history, bookmarks, cookies, saved passwords, session data, and extensions.

The locally cached data stored by a web browser to improve performance. This may include cached web pages, images, scripts, and associated metadata. The storage format varies by browser (e.g. Chrome simple cache, Firefox cache2, SQLite indexes).
Files associated with a calendar application, including events, appointments, invitations, recurring schedules, and attendee data (e.g. Apple Calendar, Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar).
Files associated with a messaging or chat application, including message databases, media attachments, contact lists, and encryption key material (e.g. WhatsApp, Signal, Telegram).
The acquisition of a clock offset measurement from a device. Contains the ClockOffsetMeasurement recording the measured difference between the device clock and a reference time source.
A timestamp observed in forensic analysis.
A cryptographic key intended for decryption.
Data produced by a device's built-in backup mechanism. Content is determined by the device's backup logic and structured in the backup's native format.
The acquisition of a screenshot from a device screen. Contains the captured image (RasterPicture).
A contextual compilation of devices that are associated in some way, such as devices belonging to the same suspect, devices seized from the same location, or devices connected to the same network.
Files associated with an email client application, including message stores, mailbox databases, attachments, contact data, and account configuration (e.g. Outlook, Apple Mail, Gmail app).
A contextual compilation of files grouped together for some purpose, such as filtering, extraction, or association with an application.

Data obtained through direct access to a file system structure. Represents the files and folders as they existed on the device or storage, applicable to any device type (mobile, desktop, embedded). Live files only.
A subset of files selected from a larger collection by some filtering criteria, such as file type, path, date range, or relevance to an investigation.

A forensic image in a container format that encapsulates acquired data, potentially compressed or encrypted, along with embedded metadata such as case information, examiner identity, acquisition timestamps, hash values, compression settings, and encryption status. It may be stored across one or more files referenced via storedIn.
A report generated by a forensic tool based on tags added during analysis.

Files associated with a gaming application, including save data, player profiles, in-app purchase records, chat logs, friend lists, and gameplay statistics (e.g. Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, Epic Games, Roblox, mobile games).
A reference set of known file hashes used to match against files under examination, in order to reduce or flag the files examined (e.g. NSRL RDS). Composed of HashSetEntry instances.
The result of comparing hash values to verify data integrity, typically comparing a source hash against a computed hash of acquired or copied data.
Files associated with a health or fitness tracking application, including activity logs, heart rate data, sleep records, workout history, and medical records (e.g. Apple Health, Google Fit, Fitbit).
A proposition or explanation put forward for consideration during forensic analysis, which may be supported or contradicted by observable artifacts.

A collection of competing alternative hypotheses considered together, for example the mutually exclusive explanations proposed for a single observation. Members are linked with solveit-analysis:hasHypothesis.

A communication that is hypothesised to have occurred between parties, potentially inferred from partial message records, contact patterns, or metadata fragments. Use uco-observable:from and uco-observable:to for the parties involved.
An event that is hypothesised to have occurred.

A relationship between entities that is hypothesised to exist, such as an inferred association between persons, accounts, devices, or locations based on co-occurrence patterns, shared identifiers, or behavioural analysis.

A web search that is hypothesised to have been performed, potentially inferred from browser history fragments, cached results, or suggested search terms. Use uco-observable:keywordSearchTerm for the search query.
An index of keywords created during forensic analysis.
Configuration settings used for keyword indexing during forensic analysis.
A result from a keyword search operation during forensic analysis.

A collection of keyword search results from a search operation. Subsequent techniques may filter or reduce this set, for example by reviewing hits, discarding false positives, or redacting privileged content. Follows the same set-based pattern as FileSet and its subclasses.
A forensic image container that encapsulates a logical collection of files rather than a bitstream copy, such as a logical image in L01 or ZIP format.
Files associated with a mapping application, including search history, saved locations, offline map tiles, and location history (e.g. Google Maps, Apple Maps, Waze).
Files associated with a turn-by-turn navigation application, including route history, recent destinations, favourite locations, and trip logs (e.g. Waze, TomTom, Garmin).
A network packet capture file.
Files associated with a mobile payment or digital wallet application, including transaction history, linked accounts, merchant data, and receipts (e.g. Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Venmo).

Files associated with a photos or gallery management application, including image and video databases, album metadata, facial recognition data, location tags, and editing history (e.g. Apple Photos, Google Photos, Samsung Gallery).
A forensic image container that encapsulates a bitstream (bit-for-bit) copy of a source medium, such as a full disk image in E01 or AFF4 format.
A device set where each device has been triaged and assigned a priority classification. Contains PrioritizedDeviceEntry instances that pair each device with its priority.

A raw forensic image containing a bitstream without container metadata. Unlike a ForensicImageContainer (e.g. E01, AFF4), a raw image has no embedded metadata. It may be stored across one or more files (e.g. split .dd segments) referenced via storedIn. Typically accompanied by a RawImageInfoFile containing hashes, case information, and acquisition details.
A logical interface to a storage device that has been interfaced with in a read-write manner, as yet, without write protection.
A collection of artifacts reduced by a redaction process to remove sensitive or privileged content before disclosure.
A subset of files reduced by a redaction process to remove sensitive or privileged content before disclosure.
Files associated with a reminders or to-do list application, including task lists, due dates, recurring reminders, and completion history (e.g. Apple Reminders, Google Tasks, Todoist).
A SQLite database file stored on disk.
A table within a SQLite database.
Data obtained by interacting with services provided by a device rather than direct storage access.

Files associated with a smart home or IoT control application, including device registries, automation routines, activity logs, sensor data, camera event histories, and network configuration (e.g. Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, Samsung SmartThings).
Files associated with a social media application, including posts, direct messages, friend/follower lists, media uploads, and notification data (e.g. Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X).
A timeline whose entries have been ordered by position, as determined by a sorting process. Multiple entries may share the same position to indicate they are tied (indistinguishable in order).
A set of timeline entries extracted during forensic analysis.
A single entry in a forensic timeline.
The computed difference between two timestamps, expressed in seconds. Positive values indicate the first timestamp is ahead of the second, negative values indicate it is behind.
A pattern used to unlock a device, i.e. screen lock pattern.
A file whose primary content is video data (e.g. MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV).

A computer (desktop, laptop, or server) that exists as a virtual machine rather than running on physical hardware. The most common form is a server running as a virtual machine in a datacentre or cloud environment, which may itself be the subject of an investigation or host evidence. In a forensic context a virtualized computer may also, for example, be a virtual machine recovered from seized media, a forensic disk image booted as a virtual machine for previewing, or a virtual machine provisioned as an analysis environment.

A list of words or terms used as input to techniques such as keyword searching or dictionary-based password attacks. May be a case-type wordlist (standard terms for a category of investigation), a case-specific wordlist (names, addresses, dates etc. specific to the investigation), or a general-purpose dictionary (e.g. for password recovery).
A logical interface to a storage device that has been interfaced with in a write-protected manner, either via a hardware write blocker, software write blocking, or a read-only boot environment.
An HTTP response header containing multiple header fields from an HTTP server response.
The date and time at which the hypothesised event is believed to have occurred - either an absolute timestamp (DateTimeStamp) or a time interval (DateTimeRange).
A device that is hypothesised to have been involved, such as a device inferred from artifacts but not yet physically identified or examined.

A user account that is hypothesised to have existed, for example inferred from recovered deleted account records, carved registry artifacts, or references to the account in other artifacts. Supporting artifacts can be linked with solveit-analysis:supportedBy.
Links a Hypothesis to artifacts that support the hypothesis.
Links a Hypothesis to artifacts that contradict the hypothesis.
Links a HypothesisSet to a member Hypothesis it groups as a competing alternative.
The name of the service or platform hypothesised to have been used (e.g. Google, WhatsApp, iMessage).
Links a ForensicToolTagBasedReport to tagged artifacts.
Links a ForensicToolTagBasedReport to tagged files.

A digital forensic technique representing how one might achieve an objective by performing an action. Based on the SOLVE-IT knowledge base. This class is a metaclass: its instances are owl:Class entities whose own instances are performed investigative actions.
A potential problem resulting from using a technique, classified according to ASTM E3016-18 error categories.
An action that can be performed to prevent a weakness from occurring or to minimize its impact.
A goal or objective in a digital forensic investigation that can be achieved through one or more techniques.

An investigative action performed as an instance of one or more SOLVE-IT techniques, recording any mitigations applied on that occasion (0..n via appliedMitigation). The technique(s) used are expressed by rdf:type against the technique class(es), not by a separate property.
Links a Technique to potential weaknesses (error categories from ASTM E3016-18) that may occur when using this technique.
Links a Technique to more specific subtechniques.
Links a Weakness to mitigations that can potentially prevent or minimize it.
Links a Mitigation to the Technique(s) it is relevant for or applies to.
Links an Objective to Techniques that can be used to achieve it.

DEPRECATED. Formerly linked a SolveitInvestigativeAction to the SOLVE-IT Technique definition(s) executed. Superseded by typing the action with the technique class itself, following the uco-action:Technique metaclass pattern.
Links a SolveitInvestigativeAction to Mitigation(s) that were actively applied during the execution to prevent or minimize potential weaknesses (0..n).
The unique identifier for a SOLVE-IT technique (e.g., T1002).
The name of the technique (e.g., 'Disk imaging').
A detailed description of how the technique is performed.
Additional details about the technique.

A CASE/UCO term that represents an expected input to this technique. Usually a class (e.g., solveit-observable:WriteProtectedDeviceInterface), but a property where the technique consumes a single value rather than an object (e.g., uco-observable:filePath). No rdfs:range is asserted, because no single one is true of both; :TechniqueIOTermShape carries the constraint instead.

A CASE/UCO term that represents an output of this technique. Usually a class (e.g., uco-observable:Image), but a property where the technique produces a single value rather than an object (e.g., case-investigation:exhibitNumber). No rdfs:range is asserted, because no single one is true of both; :TechniqueIOTermShape carries the constraint instead.
The unique identifier for a SOLVE-IT weakness (e.g., W1004).
The name describing the weakness.
A detailed description of the weakness and its potential impacts.
An error category from ASTM E3016-18 used to classify weakness impacts.
Associates a weakness with an ASTM E3016-18 error category.
The unique identifier for a SOLVE-IT mitigation (e.g., M1001).
The name describing the mitigation action.
A detailed description of how the mitigation prevents or minimizes a weakness.
The name of the objective.
A detailed description of what this objective seeks to achieve.
Academic or professional reference citation for Technique, Weakness, or Mitigation.
Alternative name or synonym for a Technique.
Example tool, implementation, or instance for a Technique.
A single frame extracted from a video file during forensic analysis.
A logical interface representing a direct connection to a storage device, such as a USB, SATA.
Access to a block device via the operating system on a live, running system. Provides sector-level access to storage without relying on the OS for file system parsing.
A contiguous run of clusters allocated to a file in a cluster-based file system (e.g., FAT, NTFS, exFAT). Multiple runs indicate file fragmentation.
An entry pairing a device with its triage priority classification.
A single entry within a hash set. At minimum it carries a hash value; further details (e.g. file name, size, product or operating system, classification) may be added as required.

A device or system that exists as a virtual machine, defined by virtualization configuration and one or more virtual disks rather than running on dedicated physical hardware. A virtualized device may arise in several ways, for example a virtual machine recovered from a suspect's storage, a forensic image booted as a virtual machine for previewing, or a virtual machine built as an analysis platform. This is the parent class for virtualized representations of any device type (e.g. computers, mobile devices).
Links a VideoFrame to the source video file.

Links a virtualized device to the file or files that constitute its virtual machine, such as a configuration file (e.g. .vmx) and one or more virtual disk files (e.g. .vmdk). Multiple files can be linked.
An ordered list of grid positions (integers) representing the unlock pattern sequence. For example, a 3x3 grid uses positions 1-9.
A device belonging to this device set.
A prioritized device entry in this set.
The device in this prioritized entry.
The triage priority classification for this device, using cacontology-forensics:priorityClassification values.
The application associated with these files.
A file belonging to this file set.
An artifact belonging to this artifact set.
Links a file to its cluster allocation runs. A contiguous file has one run; a fragmented file has multiple runs.
Links a hash set to one of the entries it contains.
The hash value carried by a hash set entry. The algorithm (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, etc.) is held within the uco-types:Hash instance via its hashMethod and hashValue.
The sequential number of this frame in the video.
Video frame width in pixels.
Video frame height in pixels.
Indicates whether the hash verification was successful (true) or failed (false).
The first cluster number in this contiguous run.
The number of contiguous clusters in this run.

A sidecar file containing metadata for a raw/dd forensic image, including hash values, case information, evidence numbers, examiner details, and acquisition notes. Compensates for the lack of embedded metadata in raw image formats.

Volatile or transient data captured from a running system at a specific point in time. Includes running processes, memory state, network connections, device interrogation data (e.g., ideviceinfo output), and system properties.

Data produced by the iOS backup mechanism via iTunes, Finder, or libimobiledevice. Contains a manifest database (Manifest.db), file blobs identified by domain-path hashes, and metadata plists including device information and backup status.
Data produced by Android's backup mechanism (e.g., adb backup). Potentially contains application data, shared storage, and system settings in the Android backup format (.ab file).
Data obtained by collecting Apple Unified Logs from a macOS or iOS device.

Data obtained from an Android device by querying content providers via an ADB shell connection (e.g., adb shell content query). Content providers expose structured data such as contacts, call logs, SMS messages, and settings without requiring direct file system access.
A file containing records generated during a data acquisition process, such as error logs or acquisition status reports.
A record of an error encountered during data acquisition such as a bad sector, read timeout, I/O error, CRC error, or media surface damage.
The logical content encapsulated within the acquired data, such as bitstream data, files, or metadata.
The source from which the data was acquired, such as a device, device interface, or storage medium.
The file or files in which the acquired data is physically stored (e.g., .E01 segment files, a .dd file, a backup archive).
Links a RawImage to its accompanying RawImageInfoFile containing metadata.
Links a forensic image container or raw image info file to errors encountered during acquisition. Multiple errors can be recorded.
Links an AcquisitionRecordFile to the error records it contains.
A hash value computed from the source device or media before or during acquisition.
A hash value computed from the acquired image or data after acquisition.
The case number stored within the forensic image container metadata.
The evidence number stored within the forensic image container metadata.
The examiner name stored within the forensic image container metadata.
The description stored within the forensic image container metadata.
The notes stored within the forensic image container metadata.
The version of the backup format used to produce the backup (e.g., iOS backup version 3.3, Android backup format v5).

Whether the backup was encrypted at the time it was generated. A backup encrypted on generation may contain a richer dataset (e.g., iOS encrypted backups include keychain and health data) even if a decrypted copy is subsequently produced.
Whether the backup is currently in an encrypted state. Used alongside encryptedOnGeneration to distinguish between a backup that is still encrypted and one that has been decrypted for analysis.
The acquisition start time as recorded in the acquisition record.
The acquisition end time as recorded in the acquisition record.
The type of acquisition error (e.g., bad sector, read timeout, I/O error, CRC error).
The starting location of the error (e.g., sector number, byte offset).
The ending location of the error (e.g., sector number, byte offset). If omitted, the error is at a single location.
Links a KeywordSearchResultSet to an individual KeywordSearchResult.
Links a KeywordIndex to its KeywordIndexingConfiguration.
A relative or implicit temporal indicator such as a sequence number, counter value, or ordering index, used when absolute timestamps are not available.

A time interval with start and end boundaries. Exactly one start property (inclusive or exclusive) and exactly one end property (inclusive or exclusive) must be specified. See SHACL shapes for validation.
The measured difference between a device clock and a reference time source. Records what was compared, the offset value, and when the comparison was made.
Links a Timeline to its TimelineEntry instances.
The temporal value of this timeline entry - an absolute timestamp (DateTimeStamp), a time interval (DateTimeRange), or relative ordering (ImplicitTimingInformation).
The device or system whose clock was measured.
The reference time source used for comparison (e.g., NTP server, GPS time, examiner's calibrated watch).
The clock offset value in seconds. Positive values indicate the clock is ahead, negative values indicate it is behind.
The specific point in time when this clock offset was determined.
The difference between two timestamps in seconds. Positive values indicate the first timestamp is ahead of the second, negative values indicate it is behind.
The date and time value of the timestamp.
The precision or resolution of the timestamp (e.g., seconds, milliseconds, microseconds).
The timezone of the timestamp.
The numeric value representing relative ordering or sequence.
The interval starts at this time (inclusive, i.e., >= this value).
The interval starts after this time (exclusive, i.e., > this value).
The interval ends at this time (inclusive, i.e., <= this value).
The interval ends before this time (exclusive, i.e., < this value).

An intermediary node that associates a TimelineEntry with its ordinal position within a SortedTimeline. This allows the same TimelineEntry to exist in both an unsorted Timeline and a SortedTimeline without duplication.
Links a sorted timeline to its sorted entry wrappers.
Links a sorted timeline entry to the original timeline entry it references.
The ordinal position of this entry within its sorted timeline. Multiple entries may share the same position to indicate they are tied (indistinguishable in order).
The schema definition for a SQLite table.
A column definition within a SQLite schema.
A physical storage page within a SQLite database file.
A record (row) within a SQLite table.
A field (cell) within a SQLite record.
A Write-Ahead Log file associated with a SQLite database.
A single frame within a SQLite WAL, containing a version of a database page.
A rollback journal file associated with a SQLite database, containing pre-modification page images.
A stored copy of a database page as it existed before modification, held in the rollback journal.
Links a SQLite database to a table it contains.
Links a SQLite database to a physical storage page.
Links a SQLite database to its Write-Ahead Log.
Links a SQLite database to its rollback journal.
Links a SQLite table to its schema definition.
Links a SQLite table to a record it contains.
Links a SQLite schema to a column definition.
Links a SQLite record to a field it contains.
The page from which this record was physically recovered.
Links a field value to its schema field definition.
Links to a CASE SQLiteBlob for binary field content. The binary content bytes are carried by a ContentDataFacet on the linked SQLiteBlob.
This page stores row data from the specified table.
This page stores B-tree structural metadata for the specified table.
Links a B-tree interior page to its child pages.
Links a WAL to a frame it contains.
Links a WAL frame to the page version it contains.
Links a rollback journal to a page image it contains.
Links a journal page image to the database page it represents the pre-modification state of.
The SQLite journal mode: DELETE, TRUNCATE, PERSIST, MEMORY, WAL, or OFF.
The column name in the schema.
The declared column type from the CREATE TABLE statement (e.g. TEXT, INTEGER, VARCHAR(20)). This may differ from the type affinity SQLite computes from it.
Zero-based position within the schema.
Whether this field is the primary key.
The page number within the database file.
e.g. b-tree leaf, b-tree interior, overflow, freelist.
The rowid of this record within its table's B-tree. Omitted for records from WITHOUT ROWID tables.
Text content of this field.
Integer content of this field.
Real number content of this field.
True if this field contains a NULL value.
The sequence number of this frame within the WAL.
The database page number that this frame contains a version of.
The database page number this image is a pre-modification copy of.
A declaration of what techniques a specific version of a tool can perform and what mitigations it implements, published by a named party. Distributed as a TTL file per tool version per publisher.
A specialised tool that has been evaluated against SOLVE-IT tool capability profiles. Adds the consultedProfile property to link an instrument to the profiles used during mitigation assessment.
A declared capability that a specific mitigation is provided by a tool, optionally subject to conditions expressed as SHACL shapes.
Enumeration of action components that conditions can evaluate against.
Links to the tool that this profile describes. That tool object also potentially contains the tool version that this applies to.
Declares that the profiled tool supports a given technique.
Links a profile to a mitigation capability declaration.
Links an instrument to the capability profiles consulted during mitigation assessment.
The SOLVE-IT mitigation that this capability implements.
A SHACL NodeShape defining the conditions for this mitigation to be active. Optional; if absent, the mitigation is unconditional.
Specifies which component of the action the condition evaluates against. Required if appliesWhen is set.
The name of the party that published this profile.
When this profile was published.
A risk assessment of a single SOLVE-IT weakness, capturing likelihood, impact, and optionally detectability ratings with computed scores.
A collection of weakness evaluations scoped to a technique or context, with authorship and date metadata. Represents one assessment session.
Links a weakness evaluation to the specific weakness being assessed.
Links an evaluation set to its constituent weakness evaluations.
Optionally scopes an evaluation set to a specific technique context.
The identity (person or organisation) that performed the evaluation.
The likelihood that this weakness will manifest. Integer score 1-3 (1=Low, 2=Medium, 3=High).
Justification for the assigned likelihood rating.
The impact if this weakness manifests. Integer score 1-3 (1=Low, 2=Medium, 3=High).
Justification for the assigned impact rating.
How difficult the weakness is to detect. Integer score 1-3 (1=Low/easy to detect, 2=Medium, 3=High/hard to detect).
Justification for the assigned detection difficulty rating.
Computed score from Likelihood x Impact (range 1-9). Low=1, Medium=2, High=3.
Risk Priority Number: Likelihood x Impact x Detection Difficulty (range 1-27). Only present when detection difficulty is rated.
Free-text context for the evaluation such as tool, platform, or case type.
Free-text rationale or caveats about the evaluation.
Descriptive label for the evaluation set.
Context or purpose of the evaluation set.
Date when the assessment was performed.

http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-.d: States that a resource is an instance of a class.
The first item in an RDF collection. Parsers produce this when expanding ( ... ) list syntax.
The remainder of an RDF collection after its first item.
The empty RDF collection, which terminates a list.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#lab.d: A human-readable name for the resource.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#com.d: A human-readable description of the resource.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#sub.d: States that all instances of one class are instances of another.
States that all resources related by one property are also related by another.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#isD.d: Indicates the resource defining the subject resource.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#see.d: Indicates a resource that may provide additional information about the subject.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#dom.d: States that any resource with this property is an instance of the named class.

http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#ran.d: States that the values of this property are instances of the named class.

http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProp.d: The class of properties whose values are individuals rather than literals.

http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypePr.d: The class of properties whose values are literals.

http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Annotation.d: The class of properties carrying annotations, which have no logical meaning.

http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#imports.d: References another ontology whose axioms this one includes.

http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#versionIRI.d: Identifies this particular version of an ontology.

http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#versionInf.d: A string describing this version of the ontology.

http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer.d: A whole number of arbitrary size.

http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#dateTim.d: An instant with date, time and optional timezone.

http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#nonNega.d: An integer of zero or greater.
